title: Geometrically connected source over a connected target implies geometric connectedness of the target
statement: Let $k$ be a field. Let $T\to X$ be a morphism of schemes over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Assume that $T$ is geometrically connected over $k$ and that $X$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

proof.text: Let $E/k$ be an arbitrary finite separable extension. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions] to the singleton family $E/k$ to obtain a finite Galois extension $L/k$ and a $k$-embedding $E\hookrightarrow L$. Thus $L$ is also a field extension of $E$. Write $f:T\to X$ for the given $k$-morphism and $f_L:T_L\to X_L$ for its base change. We will first prove $X_L$ connected, then $X_E$ connected.

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, finite Galois case; finite reduction through Tag 0389, lemma-characterize-geometrically-disconnected; Fields Tags 09DT and 0EXM (normal closure).

proof.text: By [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], $T_L$ is connected and nonempty. In particular $X_L$ is nonempty since $f_L$ maps $T_L$ to it. The morphisms $p:X_L\to X$ and $q:X_L\to X_E$ are surjective: [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective] applies to $L/k$ and $L/E$, respectively, and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] applies after base change by $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $X_E\to\operatorname{Spec}E$. For $q$ use the iterated base-change identification $X_L\simeq X_E\times_{\operatorname{Spec}E}\operatorname{Spec}L$ supplied by [def-pc-base-change].

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, connectedness of the source after extension; Morphisms Tag 01S1, lemma-base-change-surjective.

proof.text: Suppose $X_L=A\amalg B$ with $A,B$ nonempty and clopen. Their inverse images under $f_L$ form a clopen partition of the connected nonempty $T_L$, so, after interchanging $A,B$, its nonempty image $S=f_L(T_L)$ lies in $A$. For each $\sigma\in G=\operatorname{Aut}(L/k)$, let $\sigma_T=\mathrm{id}_T\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ and $\sigma_X=\mathrm{id}_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$. Functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [def-pc-base-change] gives inverse automorphisms using $\sigma^{-1}$ and $f_L\circ\sigma_T=\sigma_X\circ f_L$: both composites have $X$-projection $f$ times the $T$-projection, and $\operatorname{Spec}L$-projection $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ times the other projection. Hence $\sigma_X(S)=S$, and $S\subseteq\sigma_X(A)$ for every $\sigma$.

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, first paragraph; base-change action in equation-galois-action-base-change-kbar.

proof.text: The group $G$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field]. Set $P=\bigcap_{\sigma\in G}\sigma_X(A)$ and $Q=X_L\setminus P$. These are clopen because the intersection is finite and each $\sigma_X$ is a homeomorphism. The set $P$ is nonempty because it contains $S$; $Q$ is nonempty because the identity belongs to $G$, giving $P\subseteq A$ and $B\subseteq Q$. For $\tau\in G$, applying $\tau_X$ to $P$ just permutes its factors: the contravariance of $\operatorname{Spec}$ makes the resulting indices $\sigma\circ\tau$, which still run over all $G$. Thus both $P$ and $Q$ are $G$-invariant.

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, finite intersection and union construction; Fields Tag 09I1, lemma-finite-Galois, for finiteness of G.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-galois-invariant-closed-subset-descends] twice, to the $G$-invariant closed subsets $P,Q$ of $X_L$. Its hypotheses hold because $L/k$ is Galois, $X$ is a $k$-scheme, and its action is precisely $\sigma_X$. Obtain closed subsets $P_0,Q_0\subseteq X$ with $p^{-1}(P_0)=P$ and $p^{-1}(Q_0)=Q$. Surjectivity of $p$ from step 2 implies $P_0\cap Q_0=\varnothing$ and $P_0\cup Q_0=X$: lift a putative point in the intersection or outside the union to contradict the partition upstairs. Each is nonempty, since an element of $P$ or $Q$ projects into it. They are complements of closed subsets, hence also open. This contradicts connectedness of $X$ as defined in [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Thus $X_L$ is connected.

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, descent of the invariant partition using Tag 038B, lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois; the final contradiction.

proof.text: The surjection $q:X_L\to X_E$ from step 2 makes $X_E$ nonempty. If $X_E$ had a partition into two nonempty clopen subsets, their inverse images under the continuous map $q$ would be clopen, disjoint and covering, and each would be nonempty by surjectivity. This would contradict connectedness of $X_L$. Therefore $X_E$ is connected, using exactly the definition [def-weil-connected-scheme].

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, finite Galois argument; elementary descent of connectedness along the projection from a Galois closure.

proof.text: Since $E/k$ was arbitrary among finite separable extensions, apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-finite-separable-test] with $Y=X$. Every base change required by its right-hand condition is connected by step 6, so $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$.

source.place: Tag 056R, lemma-geometrically-connected-criterion, via Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, and Tag 0389, lemma-characterize-geometrically-disconnected.
